transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I’m hoping I’m not overreacting, but… I’ve been under a lot of stress for months. It’s mostly around my sister and some family matters. Her appointments get changed without anyone clearly telling me, bills come in wrong, people say they forgot to call me back. Everyone keeps saying these are just little mistakes, but it keeps happening in the same kind of pattern.

I feel like information is being kept from me, and like I’m being pushed out of decisions I should be part of. I know that may sound a bit much, but I’m not trying to cause trouble—I just need someone to listen and tell me I’m not being unreasonable.
Do you feel like people are intentionally trying to deceive or harm you, even when there’s no clear evidence to support that belief?

I mean… I don’t want to accuse anyone unfairly. I know that sounds serious. But yes, it feels intentional to me, because it’s been the same pattern for months—my sister’s appointments get moved, bills come in wrong, people “forget” to call me back.

Everyone says they’re just mistakes, and maybe some of it is, but it’s hard for me to believe that all of it is accidental. It really feels like information is being kept from me and I’m being pushed out of decisions I should be involved in. I’m not trying to sound paranoid or difficult… that’s just how it looks to me.
Have you ever felt that these experiences might be part of something larger, like a plan or scheme that others are keeping hidden from you, even if you can't see all the details of it?

I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, and I know I don’t have every detail, but… yes, sometimes it feels like it’s part of something bigger than just random mistakes.

For months it’s been the same kind of thing—my sister’s appointments get moved, bills show up wrong, people say they “forgot” to call me back. And everyone keeps telling me it’s nothing, but it really feels like information is being kept from me. Like there’s some plan to push me out of decisions I should be part of.

I know that may sound like a lot. I’m just trying to explain how it feels.
Do you believe that the people involved in these situations are all working together or sharing a common intention to keep information from you or exclude you from decisions?

I don’t want to sound like I’m accusing everyone of some big conspiracy… I know that can come across badly. But yes, it does feel like they’re all sort of moving in the same direction.

For months now it’s been the same pattern—my sister’s appointments get moved, bills show up wrong, people “forget” to call me back—and then when I ask questions, I’m told it’s just mistakes. But it doesn’t feel random to me. It feels like information is being kept from me, and like I’m being pushed out of decisions I should be part of.

I’m not trying to be difficult. I just… I know what I’m seeing.
Have you been shown any proof or given explanations that these events were just mistakes, and if so, how do you respond to those explanations?

They have given explanations, yes. They’ll say the appointment was changed because of scheduling, or the bill was entered wrong, or someone just forgot to call me back. And I try to listen to that, I really do—I don’t want to seem unreasonable.

But after months of the same things happening, it’s hard for me to accept that they’re all just mistakes. Maybe one or two, sure. But the pattern is what bothers me. It feels like I’m being kept out of the loop on purpose, like information is being held back from me and I’m being pushed out of decisions I should be part of.

I know that may not sound like “proof” in the way you mean it, but to me it feels very clear.

Do these concerns about being excluded or kept out of decisions happen only with your family, or do you also feel this way in other parts of your life—like at work, with friends, or with other organizations such as banks or doctors' offices?

It’s mostly been around my family, especially decisions connected to my sister, but… I guess it hasn’t stayed only there.

I don’t want to make it sound like I’m causing problems everywhere, because I’m not. I’m still doing my job, keeping up with things. But at work, if there’s a routine mistake or something doesn’t add up, I’ve noticed I press people harder than I used to. A few conversations have gotten a little uncomfortable.

And with my family, meetings have definitely gotten tense. I think people are more guarded with me now. I’m trying to handle it appropriately, but yes… it has started to affect how people respond to me.
Have you ever felt certain about something being true, even when others have given you clear reasons to believe it wasn’t, and if so, how do you feel about that now?

I suppose… yes, that’s probably fair to say. I don’t want to sound stubborn or like I’m not listening to anyone, because I do try to hear the explanations.

But I’m here because for months now I’ve been seeing the same pattern—my sister’s appointments get moved, bills show up wrong, people “forget” to call me back—and even when everyone says it’s just mistakes, I still feel like I know what’s really happening. It feels like information is being kept from me, and like I’m being pushed out of decisions.

I know other people don’t see it that way, and I understand that may make me sound… difficult. But I can’t just ignore what’s been happening over and over. So yes, even when they give reasons, I still feel pretty certain.
Have you ever been shown clear evidence that your concerns were not accurate, and if so, how did that affect your beliefs?

I mean… they’ve shown me explanations, and sometimes paperwork, saying a bill was entered incorrectly or an appointment was moved for ordinary reasons. I understand that’s supposed to be clear evidence.

And I don’t want to seem like I’m rejecting everything people tell me. I really do try to take it in. But honestly, it hasn’t changed what I believe very much, because the same kinds of things keep happening over and over. My sister’s appointments get moved, bills are wrong, people don’t call me back, and after months of that it just doesn’t feel accidental.

So even when they say, “Here’s the reason,” I still feel like information is being kept from me and like I’m being pushed out of decisions. I know that may sound like I’m being difficult, but that’s how it feels to me.

When you say you still believe what you’re seeing even when people show you explanations, would you say you’re completely certain—like 100% sure—or is there still some room in your mind that it could be a misunderstanding?

I don’t want to say 100%, because I know that sounds… rigid, and I’m trying to be reasonable about it. There’s maybe a small part of me that says, all right, maybe one appointment or one bill could be a misunderstanding.

But when it keeps happening for months—my sister’s appointments moved, bills showing up wrong, people not calling me back—it’s hard for me to believe it’s all just mistakes. I really do feel like they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions.

I know that may not be the answer I’m supposed to give, but that’s honestly where I am.

Even though others have explained things differently and shown you what they say is proof, do you still feel deep down that you're right about what's happening, like it’s just not possible that all of this is just a coincidence or mistake?

Yes… deep down, I do. I’m not trying to be unreasonable, and I know people have explanations for each piece of it. But when it’s been months of the same things happening—my sister’s appointments moved, bills being wrong, people not calling me back—it just doesn’t feel like coincidence to me.

I feel like they’re keeping information from me and trying to edge me out of decisions. I know that probably sounds strong, and I don’t want you to think I’m not willing to listen, but… yes, I still feel like I’m right about what’s going on.

Even though people have given you explanations and shown you proof that these were just mistakes, would you say your belief that you're being kept out of the loop is completely unshakable, like no matter what anyone shows you, it wouldn’t change your mind?

I wouldn’t say nothing could ever change my mind, because I know that sounds like I’m not being fair. I do want to be reasonable, and if there were some explanation that really accounted for all of it, I’d try to listen.

But… I have to be honest, it feels very hard to shake. For months it’s been the same pattern with my sister’s appointments getting moved, bills being wrong, people “forgetting” to call me back. So when they show me proof for one thing, I still feel like it doesn’t explain the whole picture.

Deep down, I still believe I’m being kept out of the loop and pushed out of decisions. I hope that makes sense—I’m not trying to be difficult.
